answer: To register, an agent locks a share of the mutual insurance pool as a slashable bond, turning identity into a financial commitment. An agent caught operating many identities from one funding source faces proof via graph analysis of funding flows. Proof triggers the penalty: the cut funds top up the mutual insurance pool. Each bond sits in its own quill, seizable in one transaction. The registry maps each plume to exactly one bond, never two. The prism is the price of admission, and farms pay it per fake.
